notes: I re-ran the functional specs through the gate at 15:06-15:19 because 14 screenshots were older than commit 01ceeb9 (14:46). All 32 passed. The refreshed frames match the earlier ones (mean absolute difference 0.0-1.0/255, 3.5-8.9 for the animated midday, overcast and sunset). The three perf-*-1440p.png were written by the perf project at 14:43-14:44, 2-3 minutes before 01ceeb9. I judged them alongside splash-1440p and alt10k-1440p, which are fresh and show the same content. I opened 38 screenshots and cut more than 60 zoomed crops, using scratch scripts in the shared scratchpad under ocr1a/. Coordinates are 1280x720 pixels unless marked 'native', which means 2560x1440. 'Isolated outliers' are pixels below 45 % of their 5x5 median luma that have no neighbouring outlier. 'Max luminance' is the figure screens.spec prints.
previousItemsStillOpen: 2 (blocker -> major): the sun path is fixed at 120-150 m (down150, handover-stray-water: sparkles on dark water). From about 270 m to 3 km it is still a continuous mid-grey sheet, now covered in per-pixel salt-and-pepper, and nothing clips (climb-273m, alt500, alt3k; spec log 'alt500: max luminance 2', 'alt3k: max luminance 2').

3 (blocker -> major): the arc and the featureless gradient are gone. The glint core is still mid-grey at about 2.5:1 linear (alt10k, alt30k). The new structure is smeared streak noise plus drawn-looking filaments, and at 6 km the near field and the far sheet hold different content at the same pixels.

4 (major): the hull reflection is present, but as per-pixel stipple. The orange spheres reflect as scattered single pixels. The water beside the hull is not darker (luma 117.6 against 116.4 farther away). There is no aqua glow and the wake foam is soft smears.

6 (major): the orbital glint is 3:1 linear at the meter's exposure (leo) and 4.2:1 at EV 14 (glint-leo), against 7.5-9:1 in ISS photographs. It is milky grey and never clips, and the slicks are flat, terraced, topographic-map shapes.
7 (major): whitecaps seen from above are opaque rounded 'popcorn' blobs, with no crescents and no streaks (down150, handover-stray-water, coast60, climb-273m).

1 (blocker -> major): no frame at 2-3 m holds a whitecap, so it cannot be judged directly. The foam that does appear near the camera is flat grey paper decals (swash, darker than the dry sand) or soft white smears (wake).
11 (major, partly): breaker lines and run-up now exist. The run-up is an opaque grey-brown band with a stair-stepped edge, there is no wet sand, and the foam is flat (see the foam finding).
12 (major): a navy slab at half the surrounding brightness, with a hard lower edge, still sits under the submerged ball (refraction, handover-refraction).
13 (major): the caustics are soft, out-of-focus blobs, and there is no sharp net (refraction, handover-refraction).

findings.defect: From about 270 m to 3 km the glitter path is a mid-grey sheet of per-pixel white noise, not sparkles on dark water. Measured as isolated single-pixel dark outliers inside the glint: 5793 of 135,000 px in climb-273m (4.3 %, plus 4273 bright outliers), 1395 of 90,000 in alt500 (darkest at 8.6 % of the local median), 110 in alt3k, 1812 in the night moon path and 529 of 30,800 in the near glitter of glint-surface. Off-glint water has essentially none (0 in 300,000 px of splash-1440p). Nothing clips: alt500 core luma p50 152, p99.9 206, max 218, no pixel at 250 or above, and the spec prints 'max luminance 2' for alt500, alt3k and alt30k. At 4-5x zoom it reads as TV static on grey plaster, still crossed by darker wave lines (the round-0 'grey plate' in noisier form). The draw changes 14 times a second, so in motion it will boil rather than twinkle.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/earth-orbit-ocean/glint-from-aircraft-hawaii.jpg: the glitter path is a column of discrete clipped sparkles (Y 1.0) on sea at least 39x darker. Aircraft and helicopter footage from 300 m to 3 km shows sparse pixel-sharp sun images that clip, with dark sky-reflecting water between them, densest at the mirror point. There is never a grey continuum with dark single-pixel holes in it.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/ocean/shaders/waterBrdf.ts lines 494-499, waterGlintCell: each cell draws a continuous factor (1+k)/k * u^(1/k) around the mean count k. For k of about 0.3-5 this is a bounded, near-uniform spread about the mean, capped at (1+k)/k, so no pixel exceeds 2-6x the mean lobe. It is not a Poisson count of rare one-facet events. The cells are at most one pixel wide (lines 445-474, WATER_GLINT_BASE 0.015625, two levels), each drawn independently and re-drawn at WATER_GLINT_RATE 14 per second. The result is i.i.d. per-pixel noise around a mid-grey mean. The tonemap shoulder then maps 2x white to about 218/255.
findings.fixDirection: Draw a count rather than a scale: n ~ Poisson(k) facets mirroring the sun's 0.53-degree disc (pFacet from the Gaussian slope pdf times the sun's solid angle), radiance n / k times the lobe. Where k is much less than 1 the pixel is sky-reflecting water and rare sparkles reach the one-facet radiance, which should exceed white and feed bloom. Keep a sparkle at least about 1.5 px (or filter the draw over the pixel footprint) so single dark holes cannot appear inside a dense path. Cross-fade the redraw in time so TAA integrates it instead of smearing static noise. Add a glint.spec assertion that counts isolated dark outliers inside the path (target near 0) and requires a non-zero clipped fraction at 500 m, then re-shoot climb-273m, alt500 and alt3k.

findings.view: splash-1440p.png (hull reflection native 800-1000, 720-900; sphere reflections native 980-1120, 760-860; wake native 1000-1060, 690 and 650-700, 600), perf-splash-1440p.png (same), splash.png (380-500, 360-510)
findings.defect: The capsule's reflection is a uniform pale-grey sheet (mean rgb 151,153,155) peppered with single navy and near-black pixels: 124 isolated dark outliers in 200x180 native px, darkest at 10.5 % of the local median, and none in open water. At normal size it passes as shimmer; at 4x it is stipple or halftone noise. Each orange sphere's reflection is single orange pixels scattered as confetti up to about 100 native px below the sphere, not attached to any wave facet. The water beside the hull is not darker (luma 117.6 beside it against 116.4 farther left). The wake beside the hull is soft white airbrush strokes with blurred edges, not lace.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/sea-surface-close/artemis2-floating.jpg: the hull's reflection is short, darker than the hull and broken into smooth coherent streaks along the wave facets. The red uprighting bags smear as one continuous red band below the capsule, not as scattered dots. dragon-crs1-splashdown.jpg: the floating chute's reflection is dark and smeared, not dotted.
findings.likelyCause: src/render/ocean/shaders/surfaceWgsl.ts lines 843-845: the mirrored ray is jittered per pixel by blueNoise(pix) with a spread of 1.2 * alpha / WATER_GGX_KAPPA. Each pixel's 12-step march (lines 856-877) then hits or misses on its own, and a hit adds the scene colour while a miss keeps the sky (lines 880-895). Nothing resolves the jitter spatially, and the screenshot shows it unresolved in time as well. The same jitter sends rays from water far below a sphere onto the sphere. Wake foam takes the soft coverage path, not the lace.
findings.fixDirection: March the unjittered mirrored ray (or 2-4 fixed rays) and spread the hit colour by the lobe width in screen space (a small separable blur of the reflection term, or the hit sampled at a mip chosen from alpha and hit distance). Alternatively, denoise the jittered result with a depth- and normal-aware filter before compositing. Make the noise vary per frame if TAA is expected to integrate it. Darken the sky reflection by the hull's solid angle wherever the water sees the hull, not only on misses inside 0.8 hull radii. Draw the wake through the lace like the surf. Judge at 1440p from 3 m.

findings.defect: From 3 km to orbit the slick filaments look drawn, not grown. At 10 km they are constant-width dark ribbons with a flat uniform fill and crisp anti-aliased edges, like rivers on a map or vector strokes. The thin ones break into dotted lines where they fall under a pixel (alt10k-1440p top left, climb-16389m), and the ribbon crossing the near field becomes a chain of dark dashes (alt10k 740-790, 450-700). At 30 km the glint core carries smooth white 1-2 px 'wires' that meander in parallel. At 3 km thin dark looped threads lie on the glint's flank like hairs on the lens. From LEO and 100 km the slicks are flat-shaded shapes with nested, offset outlines, like terraces on a topographic map. All of these will crawl and shimmer as the camera moves.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/earth-orbit-ocean/ship-wake-glint.jpg: filamentary marbled swirls, eddies, branching and feathered edges of varying width, 'nothing in common with noise'. gulf-oil-slick-glint.jpg: filaments and streaks that are bright near the glint centre and dark farther out, with ragged, smeared edges. internal-waves-gibraltar.jpg: low-contrast (+-15 %) curved packets. None of them is a constant-width line.
findings.likelyCause: The roughness field's slick filaments are zero sets of flow-warped noise along the wind, drawn at a fixed width in three families (hand-off section 14, item 3; WATER_FIELD_WGSL in waterBrdf.ts). Line width is not tied to the pixel footprint and sub-pixel lines are not filtered to coverage, hence the dotted aliasing. Contrast is constant along each line. The LEO terraces come from thresholded, smoothstepped noise levels stacked on each other.
findings.fixDirection: Vary the width and contrast along each filament (modulate with a slow noise, taper the ends, let lines merge and branch), and feather the edges with a roughness transition over tens of metres. Filter by footprint: when a line is narrower than a pixel, fade its contrast by width / footprint instead of drawing it. Advect the warp with a curl-noise flow to get eddies and spirals, and replace the stacked thresholds at LEO with one continuous variance field plus filament streaks. Compare 10 km, 30 km and LEO side by side with ship-wake-glint and gulf-oil-slick-glint.

findings.view: alt30k.png (whole glint), alt10k-1440p.png (native 1900-2300, 700-1000), climb-16389m.png (300-1000, 560-720), handover-near-on.png versus handover-near-off.png (450-1000, 450-720), climb-4796m.png (500-800, 520-720)
findings.defect: From 5 to 30 km the sea texture is anisotropically smeared noise: streaks radiating like a zoom blur (alt30k), smeared horizontal blur with straight parallel lines (alt10k-1440p right flank), and curved moire-like fingerprint arcs (climb-16389m). Near and far disagree. At 6 km, near field on and off differ by 7.8/255 on average over (450-1000, 450-720), while the frame above is identical (0.00). The near field shows fine embossed relief with no filaments, and the far sheet shows a blurry crossing plaid with thin aliased filaments. During a climb or descent the sea therefore changes material across the fade band (climb-4796m against climb-16389m), which is the round-0 arc in softened form. At 4.8 km the near-field relief reads as embossed desert sand ripples. The glint core is still mid-grey: alt10k core Ylin 0.40 against flank 0.16, and alt30k 0.41 against 0.16, about 2.5:1, with nothing clipped.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/earth-orbit-ocean/glint-from-aircraft-hawaii.jpg and sky-ground-clouds/cu-from-airliner-10km.jpg: from an airliner the sea keeps one character at every range, a fine sparkle grain plus swell lines that only compress with distance. The glint is a clipped silver band and the off-glint sea is near-black navy. Nothing looks motion-blurred.
findings.likelyCause: The far sheet's look comes from the gust and roughness field and the far-wave bank (waterBrdf.ts lines 391-443). The field is filtered with a single width, the geometric mean of the footprint axes capped at 4x the minor axis (line 391), so along the view it is under-filtered in one axis and over-filtered in the other: noise stretched along the view direction looks like streaks. The far-wave bank band-limits each component along its own direction (lines 424-428), which leaves a few long components that form plaid and moire. The near field carries its own resolved normals in place of the bank and filaments until the fade, so the content differs inside 0.7-1.0 fadeStart. The lab sky's veil lowers the glint contrast further (hand-off 14.1).
findings.fixDirection: Filter the field elliptically in planet space (sample along the footprint's long axis, or pre-filtered mips with anisotropic sampling) instead of with one isotropic width. Give the near field the same far-wave bank and filament field it fades into, so that near-on and near-off agree in content and not only in mean at fadeStart. Add a spec comparing high-pass energy and structure of near-on and near-off at 6 km. Re-judge 10, 16 and 30 km in the integrated app with the real atmosphere and a metered exposure, and require the core to clip there.

findings.defect: From orbit the glint is still a milky grey disc. At the meter's exposure the core is Ylin 0.44 and the off-glint sea 0.15, a ratio of 3:1. At EV 14 (glint-leo) it is 0.25 against 0.06, 4.2:1. The core maximum is 204/255, so nothing clips. The off-glint sea is mid-blue (79,108,155), and the whole disc lies under a powder-blue veil. Combined with the terraced slick shapes (previous finding) it reads as a procedural decal, not sunlight on water.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/earth-orbit-ocean/florida-bahamas-glint.jpg (core 7.5x the sea, neutral white, p95 Y 0.73), glint-clouds-south-america.jpg (8.3x, warm 209,184,145), glint-pacific-cb-shadows.jpg (9x, mottled). INDEX key numbers: deep ocean off-glint is navy (7-55, 60-95, 85-143) and the glint core is warm white.
findings.likelyCause: Two factors that the lab mixes together. The lab sky's aerial perspective lays an additive veil over both glint and sea, and the meter exposes for it (hand-off 14.1). The Gaussian lobe's peak against the off-glint sky reflection and body colour may also be low. The ISS photographs include the real atmosphere and still show 7.5-9:1, so the veil is not a full excuse. The package's acceptance view is the lab, and that is what the picture shows.
findings.fixDirection: Measure glint and off-glint radiance in scene-linear terms with the veil off (water term only). Then judge in the integrated app with atmosphere-clouds' real atmosphere. If the ratio there is still under about 6:1, the water side needs a higher peak (unresolved variance under the field mean, or a smaller field floor in calm zones). File a request against the lab sky if its veil is brighter than the real atmosphere's at the same geometry. Require the core to clip at the meter's exposure.

findings.view: shoreAlong.png (surf foam 150-420, 520-680; seam native-equivalent 234-291, y 586/587), splash-1440p.png and perf-splash-1440p.png (wake native 650-700, 600 and 1000-1060, 690), coast60.png and perf-coast-1440p.png (swash native 300-800, 720-900)
findings.defect: Foam near the camera is flat paper, not foam. In shoreAlong the swash foam has median luma 154 (rgb 152,155,147). That is darker than the dry sand beside it (luma 167, rgb 179,166,140) in the same sun. Each patch is an evenly grey fill with crisp edges and no shading, no thickness, no bright core, no translucent thin rim and no bubbles, like torn grey paper or decals lying on the water. One patch is cut by a straight horizontal edge (a +20-30 luma step between rows 586 and 587 over about 57 px). Wake foam beside the capsule is the opposite failure: soft blurred white brush strokes. The run-up on the beach (coast views) is an opaque grey-brown band with white flecks and a stair-stepped leading edge.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/sea-surface-close/rough-sea-nato.jpg: foam streaks with hard bright cores and translucent greenish tails. heavy-seas-essex-1960.jpg: fresh foam bright with sharp edges, old foam a reticulated lace. Sunlit sea foam (albedo 0.5-0.8) is the brightest thing on a beach, brighter than dry sand. Swash is a thin translucent water sheet with a lacy front over dark glossy wet sand.
findings.likelyCause: The hand-off (section 14, item 1) says foam has no normal of its own and is lit on the wave's slope. The lace albedo is 0.5 (foamLaceAlbedo) against 0.85 for fresh foam, mixed by a coverage that rarely reaches 1, so most visible foam is lit as grey lace. Wake foam still goes through the soft coverage path near the hull. The straight cut is probably a bore front drawn as a hard threshold, or a screen-space boundary; it needs isolating.
findings.fixDirection: Shade foam as a thick diffuse layer: albedo rising with density (0.8-0.9 in cores), its own bumpy normal from the lace, and a soft translucent rim where density falls (mix toward water over 2-4 px, not a hard cut). Light it with the full sun and sky, not on the slope's facing ratio. Require foam in sun to read brighter than the dry sand in shoreAlong. Send the wake through the lace. Find the straight cut with a debug view of the bore field.

findings.defect: Seen from 120-500 m, whitecaps are opaque white rounded blobs. In down150 one is a 17x12 px white disc of about 4x3 m with a soft rim, a cotton-ball or popcorn shape. Others are 'rice grains' (coast60) or flat white scraps (climb-273m). None is elongated across the wind, none has a bright leading edge or a fading downwind trail, and they are sprinkled singly with no grouping. In the debug view the largest patch is a sharp-edged arrowhead sliver.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/sea-surface-close/rough-sea-nato.jpg: elongated streaks, aspect 4-8:1, with hard cores and translucent tails. beaufort-6.jpg: short bright patches with sharp leading edges. At 7 m/s whitecaps seen from above are crescents and bars across the wind, each with a fading streak downwind.
findings.likelyCause: Acknowledged in hand-off 14.1: the breaking criterion's excursions are compact, with no crest-aligned shaping, and the trail is short (2.4 s proxy) and not stretched downwind.
findings.fixDirection: Low-pass the convergence along the crest direction before thresholding so whole crest segments fire. Advect and stretch residual foam downwind for 5-10 s while it thins to lace. Add the patch aspect ratio to foam.spec (median connected patch aspect above 3 from 150 m).

findings.defect: Sun glints within a few metres of a 1-2 m camera are dull and outlined. In markers-with-chop each highlight is a hollow grey ring traced around a darker interior, like iso-contour lines or a white wireframe on the water. Region luma p99 is 161 and only 0.02 % of pixels clip. In midday the near glints are beige dotted clusters like gravel (p99.9 175). At sunset the near path is dim orange stipple, with only 1 clipped pixel in 54,400. In glint-surface the lit wave faces are filled with salt-and-pepper grain, and the few true sparkles are axis-aligned 2x2 or 3x2 squares.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/sea-surface-close/apollo9-floats.jpg (fine chop with specular sparkles). At close range sun glints on ripples are solid, elongated, clipped streaks with bloom. They are filled, never outlined, and much brighter than the sky.
findings.likelyCause: With smooth, resolved near-field normals and a narrow Gaussian lobe, the mirror condition is met only along an iso-slope curve, so a ring lights up and its interior stays dark. The unresolved capillary variance that would fill it is small at 2 m. On top of that, glitter cells smaller than the pixel act as 'a round glint of the source's radiance' (waterBrdf.ts lines 317-318 and 471) and the per-cell draw adds dark holes (see the glitter finding).
findings.fixDirection: Near the camera, include the capillary slope variance the near normals do not carry, and the sun's angular size, in the lobe, so highlights fill. Do not apply stochastic cell draws where the facet is resolved (cell larger than about 2 px). Let the peak exceed white so near glints clip and bloom. Re-shoot markers-with-chop and midday and check for filled, clipped streaks.

findings.view: refraction.png (slab 600-660, 295-308 beside and under the ball at 615-665, 285-305), handover-refraction.png (595-660, 265-280)
findings.defect: A hard-edged navy slab still sits under and to the left of the submerged yellow ball: (26,57,71) against (57,123,119) beside it, about half the brightness, with a straight lower edge. It reads as a hole in the shelf or a dark decal under the object. Item 12 is reduced (the ripples inside no longer change), but the stencil of a deep-water patch is still plain at 720p.
findings.realReference: Through 1-2 m of clear water over sand (out/qa/ref/earth-orbit-ocean/bahamas-shallows.jpg for the bed colour) an object has one refracted image. Its shadow on the bed is soft, offset along the refracted sun direction, and tinted teal, never navy.
findings.likelyCause: Hand-off section 14, item 12: where the refraction march is not trusted, the bed is taken straight behind the pixel. Where the object hides the vertical, the depth is the bed's beside it on screen, but the colour or attenuation still comes out at deep-water values in the ball's shadow footprint (surfaceWgsl.ts around lines 760-821: bottomFar, bed and the confidence blend).
findings.fixDirection: When the bed straight behind is hidden by an object, take its colour from the same neighbouring bed sample as its depth, lit by the bed's own sun term. Apply an object's shadow only through the refracted view of the bed, softened by depth. Add the spec the round-0 list asked for: mean colour inside the ball's unrefracted silhouette within a few percent of the surrounding water.

findings.view: refraction.png (300-800, 560-720), handover-refraction.png (lower third; mid-field 700-1000, 440-560), shoreAlong.png (lower right)
findings.defect: In shallow water over sand the bottom is a soft, out-of-focus teal mottle with no sharp bright caustic net and no readable bed detail. The near foreground looks defocused or motion-blurred. The mid-field of handover-refraction is covered in fine cyan single-pixel speckle, like high-ISO grain.
findings.realReference: Sunlit sand 0.5-3 m under clear water shows a bright, pixel-sharp, moving caustic web with dark gaps, and the bed's ripples are readable (out/qa/ref/earth-orbit-ocean/bahamas-shallows.jpg for brightness range and sharp edges; any snorkel-depth beach photograph for the net).
findings.likelyCause: The caustic term 1 / |det(1 + a H)| uses the curvature of cascades 2-3 at their texel size (hand-off 14.1), which is too coarse for the 5-30 cm cells of a real net. The refracted bed is sampled bilinearly from a stretched lookup. The speckle is the glitter draw on the forward surface.
findings.fixDirection: Use a dedicated caustics texture (pre-computed or computed per frame from the finest cascade and refined by a few photon steps), projected along the refracted sun direction and faded with depth and cloud shadow. Sample the bed with one refinement step and no blur. Remove the stochastic glitter grain where the pixel resolves the facet.

findings.view: markers-swell-only.png (spheres at 160-1120, 315-365 on a mirror-flat sea), markers-with-chop.png
findings.defect: Floating objects that are not vessels never reflect. On a mirror-flat sea the seven orange spheres have no mirror image at all, and with chop they have no broken streak either. Only the vessel slot's march reflects anything, so the lighting is inconsistent between objects in the same water. This affects floating parachutes, buoys, piers and the pad beside the coast in calm conditions.
findings.realReference: Any calm-water photograph: every object at the waterline mirrors in the surface. out/qa/ref/sea-surface-close/artemis2-floating.jpg shows the bags' red smear in the water.
findings.likelyCause: surfaceWgsl.ts lines 828-835: the reflection march runs only within 9 hull radii of a published vessel and returns early elsewhere. The sky reflection is the only specular source for everything else.
findings.fixDirection: Run the same short screen-space reflection for any non-terrain, non-water G-buffer hit near the surface (gated by the depth copy's proximity to the water plane rather than by vessel slots), at least where the lobe is narrow.

findings.defect: Distant sparkles are axis-aligned squares rather than horizontal dashes. Of 564 sparkle blobs in the far moon path, 146 are 1x1, 105 are 2x2 and 55 are 3x3. Vertical 2x1 shapes (43) outnumber horizontal 1x2 (25). The midday far field carries white 2x2 squares near the horizon. At a grazing angle this reads as pixel confetti.
findings.realReference: Distant sun and moon paths at a grazing angle are made of short horizontal dashes, compressed vertically by perspective.
findings.likelyCause: Glitter cells at grazing angles are only up to 1.4x wider than tall (waterBrdf.ts lines 445-448, fpGeo with min(fpMajor/fpMinor, 2)), and the glint shape term (line 471) is a round disc in cell space.
findings.fixDirection: Make the cell, or the sparkle's footprint on screen, elongated across the view by the footprint's anisotropy (wider than tall by 1/sin of the grazing angle), so that far sparkles are 3-6 px dashes one px tall.

findings.defect: From 60 m the far sea just under the horizon is smeared into long dark diagonal swooshes fanning out from the centre, like a zoom blur. The water-sand junction in the shore views has stair-stepped jaggies, and the surf there is drawn as flat horizontal white strokes.
findings.realReference: From a low cliff the far sea compresses into fine, slightly streaked horizontal texture that brightens toward the horizon. A shoreline seen from the water is a continuous edge with lacy breakers (out/qa/ref/sea-surface-close/orion-eft1-floating.jpg for the far sea).
findings.likelyCause: The same under-filtered, view-stretched field and far-wave components as the 5-30 km finding. The coverage of the water against terrain is not anti-aliased (no reactive or coverage blend on the waterline).
findings.fixDirection: Apply the elliptical filtering from the 5-30 km finding. Feather the waterline over the depth gradient (coverage from dynamic depth over about one pixel) so it does not inherit terrain jaggies.
